assumptions: the full field spaces and SO(9) action are unchanged
spatial SO(9) commutes with the time derivative D
retract maps are matrices over a characteristic-zero derivative ring
equivariance is strict rather than modulo gauge transformations
coefficient_argument: For T(D)=sum_k T_k D^k, C_target T(D)=T(D) C_source gives (c_target-c_source) T_k=0 for every k. Each displayed difference is a nonzero real scalar and hence a unit in both rings.
conclusion: Ordinary node raising, lowering, and even Laurent powers of the time derivative cannot cure the SO(9) Casimir mismatch while the 128|128 field module is fixed. A surviving route must change the representation content or weaken strict equivariance through a gauge/Bianchi quotient.
